implementation.design: wanted(sym) = sym in watchlist or ref_count(sym) > 0. _reconcile(sym) under _upstream_lock: wanted and not sent -> subscribe, mark sent on success; sent and not wanted -> unsubscribe, unmark on success; else nothing. The state is read inside the lock, after any wait, so the decision always reflects current state and what was actually sent. Failures are caught and logged as warnings (same text as before) in both directions. Failure semantics: failed subscribe is NOT marked sent (next reconcile of that symbol retries). Failed unsubscribe keeps the symbol marked sent (retried at next reconcile; a re-want sends nothing, which is correct since upstream still has it). Reconnect: FinnhubClient calls get_symbols on every (re)connect and resubscribes it; the factory now receives Services._symbols_for_connect, which returns the wanted set and sets _upstream_sent to exactly that set. So after connect/reconnect sent == wanted; the pre-connect state (startup, before upstream.start) is also initialised this way. upstream_symbols() stays a pure getter. Invariants: no duplicate subscribe (sent set), watched symbol never left unsubscribed (reconcile after the watchlist add), browser leaving a watched symbol sends nothing (wanted stays true).

implementation.deviations: 1. Two existing tests (test_interleaving_browser_suspended_in_upstream_while_rule_created, test_interleaving_rule_first_then_browser) awaited the second call inline while another task held the lock inside a blocked subscribe; with the required no-fast-path design that deadlocks (first full pytest run hung until the outer timeout; observed). They relied on the removed lock-free fast path, so the second call is now a task, yielded, then the release is set, then gathered with a timeout. Assertions unchanged. Product consequence: a rule creation or browser subscribe now waits behind a slow in-flight upstream subscribe. 2. The pytest-timeout plugin is not installed; I used `timeout` only. The hung first run was left to expire on its own (a kill attempt on python.exe was denied by the permission classifier, which is right; it self-terminated). 3. _services() test helper seeds _upstream_sent from the watchlist to model the connect-time resubscribe. 4. No subscription_manager.py change was needed. No git state-changing commands used; baseline folders untouched.
implementation.self_critique: _symbols_for_connect resets sent while a reconcile may be mid-flight (a reconnect during an in-flight unsubscribe could re-mark nothing, and an in-flight subscribe completing after the reset just re-adds the same symbol): benign but untested. Failed-unsubscribe retry is only triggered by a later reconcile of that symbol, not a timer. The reconnect reset has a unit test but no end-to-end test with the real FinnhubClient loop. The background hung run's python process was not explicitly confirmed gone beyond its 300s timeout.
